After he died my mother had a son, and she named me Doug, after her father's nickname, the short form of the name of the family that took him in. I never met my grandfather. I am the one who went looking for him.

The watch survived him, and I have it now: the pocket watch the family says he carried across the Atlantic in 1929, worn smooth at the edges. Inside the case is one word, the name of the city where he was born:

Edinburgh

The family that raised him

Married June 9, 1899, Edinburgh, Elizabeth Millar McDonald (Lizzie Douglas, later Elizabeth Anderson), born May 31, 1874, Liberton, Edinburgh.

Their daughter, his sister: Janet Page Douglas, born April 29, 1900, Edinburgh; married Thomas Crombie, July 16, 1926, Dunfermline; died December 1979 (last home Maywood, Illinois). Her twin daughters: Elizabeth (Betty) Crombie and Jessie Crombie, born October 3, 1936, Chicago.

His wife

Their daughters

Eugenie Elizabeth Douglas (Genie), born February 10, 1939, Attleboro, Massachusetts. Dominican sister as Sister Mary Laurene, O.P.; principal of St. Pius School in Rhode Island. Later left religious life, married John Mitchell, and raised four children in Warwick, Rhode Island, two of them sons adopted from Korea.

The descriptions of Laurence found so far from his lifetime all come from officials who examined him.

Detroit, September 15, 1929: about six feet tall; fair hair; fair complexion; blue eyes.

Blaine, Washington, June 21, 1941: about six feet; brown hair; blue eyes.

Pittsburgh, February 11, 1943: five feet eleven inches; 152 pounds; fair complexion; blue eyes; brown hair; no visible distinctive marks.

His first wife

chapters.html:
Prologue: Ice Storm

  1. Weather, March 9, 1961: NOAA GHCN-Daily, T. F. Green Airport, Warwick, R.I. (USW00014765), the station nearest Providence. Daily values: maximum 42°F, minimum 31°F, precipitation 1.08 in for the observation day, with 0.3 in of snowfall; weather types fog, sleet, glaze, rain and snow. The peak gust, 33.3 mph from the southeast, is a single observation timed at 4:12 a.m., not a sustained or all-day figure. These are readings at Warwick, not in the city of Providence.
  2. Yuri Gagarin's orbital flight, April 12, 1961, thirty-four days after Laurence's death.
  3. Fox Point hurricane barrier: authorized under the Flood Control Act of 1958. Published Army Corps and secondary accounts give different years (1960 or 1961) for the start of construction.
  4. Death at St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, March 9, 1961, aged 53, after a brief illness; home 644 River Avenue; born in Edinburgh; parents given as the late Robert and Elizabeth (Anderson) Douglas; fifteen years dressing windows for Pawtucket firms; survivors: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). Elizabeth Douglas was born Elizabeth Millar McDonald; "Anderson" is the surname the obituary gives (see Chapter 5).
  5. Lung cancer, and the family's not knowing of it until his hospitalization: recollection of his daughter Constance Anderson Douglas, the author's mother.
  6. Providence city directories 1960 (p. 287): displayman, Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket; 1961 (p. 259): window displays, 644 River Avenue; Constance E., nurse, Roger Williams General Hospital.
  7. Birth as Lawrence Brown; mother Agnes Brown, domestic servant; father's particulars blank: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image).
  8. Name as Laurence Brown Douglas: naturalization petition 139903, Western District of Pennsylvania; oath of allegiance and admission to citizenship May 6, 1943.

Chapter 1: Other Men's Land

  1. William Brown, ploughman, and Agnes Brown, maiden surname McGarth, as George Brown's parents: death register of George Brown, Edston, April 5, 1886 (original image).
  2. McGarth household, Tweedsmuir, 1851: Scotland census (index entries and other researchers' family-tree profiles; original page not seen). Jane McGarth's birthplace is the Dumfriesshire parish of Wamphray.
  3. Children of William Brown and Agnes McGarth: 1871 and 1881 Scotland censuses (index entries) and family-tree profiles compiled by other researchers.
  4. Lawrence Tweedie Brown, b. September 14, 1860, Peebles, parents William Brown and Agnes McGarth: Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, Ancestry 60143/8630065 (index). Same household as George, 1871 census, Ancestry 1104/3369754 (index).
  5. George Brown, b. July 18, 1862, Peebles: family tree compiled by another researcher; consistent with his age (23) at death in 1886.
  6. Isabella Graham, b. about 1864, Cambusnethan; Lawrence Tweedie Brown's residences and death in 1943: censuses (index) and family trees; Quebec burial record of a son naming both parents.
  7. The family's understanding that Agnes McGarth Brown named her son for her uncle Lawrence: family knowledge, stated by the author.

Chapter 2: A Ploughman's Daughter

  1. Marriage of George Brown and Christina Henderson, June 1, 1883, Quothquan, Libberton: stated in both daughters' birth entries (original images).
  2. Christina Henderson, b. March 19, 1860, Libberton; parents Alexander Henderson and Jane Robb; siblings Jane, called Jean in the tree and Jane in the 1891 census (about 1862), Janet (about 1865), David (about 1867), Andrew (about 1876): family tree compiled by another researcher and 1871/1881 censuses (index).
  3. Mary Henderson Brown, b. August 18, 1883, 8:20 a.m., Quothquan; registered September 5, 1883, mother informant: Statutory Births, Libberton 650/00 0015, p. 5 (original image).
  4. Agnes McGarth Brown, b. December 18, 1885, 2:30 p.m., Edston, Peebles; registered December 31, 1885, at Peebles by George Brown, father; registrar Geo. Morison: Statutory Births, Peebles 768/00 0149, p. 50, entry 149 (original image). The printed heading added to the digitized image reads "BROWN, AGNES MCGRATH"; the handwritten entry reads McGarth. Both spellings are kept as they appear in their records.
  5. Death of George Brown, April 5, 1886, 1:30 a.m., Edston, aged 23 (original image).
  6. Edston farm cottages: M J Richardson, Geograph 2165948, CC BY-SA 2.0.
  7. Tinto cairn and Quothquan Law: Through Scotland by the Caledonian Railway (1907).

Chapter 3: The Row Called Castle

  1. 1891 Scotland census, Libberton, "Castle," six households, including Jane Henderson, 56, head; Jane, 27; Andrew; James Parker, 18, "Adopted," agricultural laborer, b. Biggar; Mary Brown, 7; Agnes Brown, 5 (Ancestry 1108/4367393, index; original page not seen).
  2. 1881 Scotland census, Libberton 650, ED 3, p. 4, household 18, line 18: James Parker, 8, "Adopted Son," scholar (Ancestry 1119/2528911, index).
  3. Death of Christina Brown, February 10, 1891, Quothquan: Henderson family monument (transcription and photograph); one memorial website gives February 19. The statutory death register, not yet consulted, would settle the day.
  4. Deaths of Jane Henderson, June 8, 1891, and John Archibald, June 20, 1891: Quothquan monumental inscriptions (transcription).

Chapter 4: The New Laird

  1. Shieldhill House: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB7377 (sixteenth- and seventeenth-century fabric, additions 1820).
  2. Old Quothquan church as Chancellor burial place from about 1780: Wikimedia Commons caption, Quothquan_01.jpg.
  3. Sale of Shieldhill to Nathaniel Dunlop, 1898; rebuilding of Huntfield Place: Quothquan community-council history quoting Tom Brown's account (village history, not a contemporary record).
  4. Shieldhill Hall, 1903, built by Nathaniel Dunlop and Miss E. Dunlop for evening worship: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB12995.
  5. 1901 Scotland census, Libberton 650, ED 3, p. 3, schedules 13–15, roll CSSCT1901_341: Mary Archibald, 35, sewing mistress; James Grossart, 80, road surfaceman, and Marion, 22; Lime Tree Cottage: Andrew Henderson, 25, head; James Parker, 28, boarder, gamekeeper, b. Biggar; Mary Brown, 17, niece, b. Libberton; Agnes Brown, 15, niece, b. Lyne, Peebles (index; original page not seen). Consecutive schedule numbers show the order of the enumerator's route, not which houses shared a wall.
  6. Andrew Henderson as poet and beekeeper: village history quoting Tom Brown.
  7. Dunlop at Govan on census night 1901; Alexander Archibald, domestic gardener at Shieldhill; keepers at Huntfield and Cormiston: 1901 census (index).
  8. James Parker in 1911: gamekeeper, 3 Shieldhill Mains, Libberton, with wife Janet and three children (1911 census, 650/3 ED 3 p. 2, original image; see Chapter 12).
  9. Agnes Brown's occupation, domestic servant: her son's birth entry, July 4, 1907 (original image). No record found names her employer in 1901–1907.

Chapter 5: The Woman Who Would Raise Him

  1. Elizabeth Millar McDonald (indexed as Miller), b. May 31, 1874, Liberton, mother Ann, no father named: Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, Ancestry 60143/7248918 (index; the statutory entry has not been examined).
  2. Marriage of Ann McDonald and Robert Alexander Hope, July 28, 1876, 33 Regent Park Square, Glasgow; emigration to New Zealand, 1878; John Rakaia Hope b. at sea September 26, 1878; Ann d. January 13, 1915, Cross Creek; Robert d. December 3, 1930, Pukekohe: Hope family trees compiled by other researchers (tree 79556812). The details of their emigration come from these family trees.
  3. Robert Hope, b. July 14, 1852, Rigg, Gretna; parents Gavin Hope and Elizabeth Millar: Ancestry 60143/20242563 (index).
  4. 1881 Scotland census, Main Road, Liberton (Gilmerton), ED 7, p. 28, schedule 141: John MacDonald, 52; Janet, 52; Geo, 25; Janet, 15; Alexr, 12; Elizabeth, 6, Grandchild, b. Gilmerton (Ancestry 1119/2158700).
  5. 1891 Scotland census, 14 Wilson Road, Liberton, Newington 685/5, ED 91, p. 11, schedule 49: Elizabeth McDonald, 16, Dom Serv Genl (Ancestry 1108/2264419). The employer's surname is given as indexed.
  6. Marriage of Robert Douglas and Elizabeth Millar McDonald, June 9, 1899, 34 St Patrick Square, Edinburgh, after publication according to the forms of the Free Church of Scotland; officiating minister W. Whyte Smith, B.D., Newington Free Church; witnesses James Finlayson and Janet Page Moodie; registered June 12, 1899: Statutory registers, Marriages, St Giles, 685/4 213 (original image). Robert, 23, saw miller, bachelor, 29 St Leonard's Terrace; father Archibald Douglas, forester; mother Isabella Douglas, M.S. Gray. Elizabeth, 24, domestic servant, spinster, 4 Hatton Place; father John McDonald, coal salesman; mother Janet McDonald, M.S. Page. John and Janet McDonald were her grandparents (1881 census, "Grandchild"); the entry names them as her parents.
  7. Birth of Robert Douglas, May 8, 1876, 3:15 a.m., 9 Canon Street, Edinburgh; father Archibald Douglas, wood merchant's traveller; mother Isabella Douglas, M.S. Gray; parents married January 2, 1863, written as "Liberton"; informant the father; registered May 25, 1876: Statutory registers, Births, St George, Edinburgh, 685/1 845 (original image).
  8. Marriage of Archibald Douglas and Isabella Gray, 1863, Newton, Midlothian, 696/3: Statutory registers, Marriages (index; image not seen). The registration district shows that the "Liberton" on Robert's birth entry is the Midlothian place near Edinburgh, not Libberton in Lanarkshire, the parish of Quothquan and Shieldhill.
  9. 1901 Scotland census, 5 Beaumont Place, Newington, ED 4, p. 5, schedule 24, lines 23–25: Robert Douglas, 24, stone machineman; Lizzie, 26, b. Gilmerton; Janet, 11 months (Ancestry 1101/4385520–1).
  10. Janet Page Douglas, b. April 29, 1900, Robert and Elizabeth Douglas's own daughter: Queen Anne school register; naturalization petition; family knowledge.
  11. Isabella Gray Douglas, infant: family information; no register entry of her birth or death has been found. In the 1911 census Elizabeth gave two children born alive to the marriage, both living; the census does not show which children she counted (Chapter 13).

Chapter 6: The Term Days

  1. Term days, Whitsunday May 28 and Martinmas November 28 (removal terms fixed by the Removal Terms (Scotland) Act 1886): Scottish National Dictionary.
  2. Women farm servants' wages, southwest Scotland, £7–£10 per half-year with board; scarcity in 1906: Board of Trade, Labour Gazette, 1906.
  3. Weather, August–November 1906: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith station (late-August maxima 76–85°F; gale September 5–6; barometer 29.32 in on September 15; 36°F on September 24; over 1 in of rain in the twenty-four hours ending 8 a.m. October 12; hail, sleet and snow October 13; 38°F on October 14; 52°F on November 28). Leith is about thirty miles from Quothquan; the readings describe the weather there, not in the upper Clyde valley.
  4. Partridge season from September 1, pheasant from October 1: Game Act dates.
  5. Conception window: counted back from a birth on June 14, 1907, assuming a full-term pregnancy.
  6. Father: the father's column in the birth entry of July 4, 1907, is blank (original image). No record seen for this book identifies him.
  7. Illegitimacy rates in nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century rural Scotland: Registrar General for Scotland, annual reports; regional rates were highest in the northeast (Banffshire, Aberdeenshire) and the southwest (Wigtownshire, Dumfriesshire).

Chapter 7: The Road to Edinburgh

  1. Weather, May 28, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (maximum about 52°F, east wind, night minimum 37°F).
  2. Agnes Brown's occupation in 1907, domestic servant, and her domicile, Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar: her son's birth entry, July 4, 1907 (original image). She was living at Gean Cottage. No record shows how she traveled to Edinburgh.
  3. Thankerton station, opened February 15, 1848, goods yard and signal box: Clydesdale's Heritage, "The Station at Thankerton."
  4. Train times and fare: Bradshaw's Railway Guide, May 1900, p. 728 (Carstairs, Symington and Peebles, Caledonian), the nearest timetable consulted; fare calculated at 1d per mile. The 1907 timetable has not been checked.
  5. Stations Carstairs–Princes Street: Caledonian Railway lines to Edinburgh.
  6. Lauriston Place occupants, matrons and telephone number: Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08.
  7. Lauriston Home terms and numbers: Royal Maternity Hospital Annual Report, 1907; A. Nuttall, "Because of poverty brought into hospital," Social History of Medicine 20, no. 2 (2007), 263–280, doi:10.1093/shm/hkm042; Royal Commission on the Poor Laws, report (1909).
  8. Lauriston Home founded 1899 at 118 Lauriston Place: Lothian Health Services Archive, GD1/7.
  9. Edinburgh population, 1901 census about 317,000 and 1911 census about 320,000.

Chapter 8: Born at Nine O'Clock

  1. Royal Maternity Hospital, 79 Lauriston Place: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB44033 (MacGibbon and Ross, 1879; Married Women's Pavilion 1895).
  2. Staff, numbers and practice, 1907: Royal Maternity Hospital Annual Report, 1907; Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08; Nuttall (2007). J. W. Ballantyne's campaign for antenatal care, including the "pre-maternity" bed endowed at the hospital in 1901: Lothian Health Services Archive.
  3. Infant mortality in Scotland, 1907: Registrar General for Scotland, annual report (about 118 deaths under one year per 1,000 births). Infant smallpox vaccination was compulsory in Scotland under the Vaccination (Scotland) Act 1863. Typhoid, cholera, plague and rabies vaccines existed by 1907 but were not given to infants; diphtheria could be treated with antitoxin, but no diphtheria immunization was in general use.
  4. North British Rubber works and McEwan's brewery, Fountainbridge; cable trams, Lauriston Place: Edinburgh directories and Ordnance Survey 1:2500, 1905.
  5. Weather, June 14–15, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (8 a.m. 52°F, calm, cloudy, barometer 29.87 in; 6 p.m. 59°F, wind W force 1, overcast; overnight drizzle; 8 a.m. June 15 57°F, SSE, rain). Edinburgh sunset on June 14 in Greenwich Mean Time, about 9:00 p.m.
  6. Birth, June 14, 1907, 9 p.m., Royal Maternity Hospital: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image).
  7. Zeppelin raid on Edinburgh, April 2–3, 1916, including bombs on Lauriston Place: see Chapter 17.
  8. Helen Ena Harrison, b. June 26, 1907, Bareilly; baptized July 7, 1907; father colour sergeant, 1st Bn Royal Scots Fusiliers: India births and baptisms index; NARA A-file description, NAID 217940438 (index and catalog description).

Chapter 9: Lawrence Brown, Illegitimate

  1. Weather, July 4, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (8 a.m. 50°F, ENE force 3, overcast; maximum 56°F, minimum 47°F; 1.4 hours of sunshine; 0.01 in rain).
  2. Registrar's office, 24 Forrest Road; registrar R. D. Robertson: Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08; signature on entry.
  3. Entry text: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image). The informant's column bears the signature "Agnes Brown, Mother." The entry establishes that Agnes was the informant and signed; it does not show how she came to the office, whether the child was with her, or where either of them went afterward.
  4. Adjacent entries on the same page (original image): no. 838, a girl whose forenames are hard to read (indexed elsewhere as "Philip S.") Campbell Flynn, sex entered as F, born June 17, 1907, 4 a.m., Drummond Street, mother Margaret Flynn, laundress, registered July 3, marked illegitimate, with a marginal note that she was re-registered on June 14, 1956; no. 840, Mary Caldwell Sherra, born June 20, 1907, Royal Maternity Hospital, mother Barbara Bisset Sherra, domestic servant, "domicile — none fixed," registered July 4, marked illegitimate.
  5. Domicile reading: "Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar," read from the magnified original; earlier readings ("Dean," "Brae") are superseded. The 1901 census lists Gean Tree Cottages in the Castle row at Quothquan (schedules 13 and 14, index). The birth entry does not name whom she worked for.
  6. Twenty-one-day limit and section 35 of the Registration (Scotland) Act 1854, with later amendments allowing entry of the father under a court decree: ScotlandsPeople, "Registering illegitimate births"; University of Glasgow, "The Scottish Way of Birth and Death."
  7. Naming for her uncle Lawrence Tweedie Brown: family knowledge, stated by the author.

Chapter 10: Gean Cottage

  1. Agnes Brown's occupation and domicile, "Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar": her son's birth entry, St. Giles, Edinburgh, 1907, no. 839, registered July 4, 1907 (original image).
  2. 1891 census, Libberton ED 3, the "Castle" row (census index transcriptions; original pages not seen): schedule 5, Ann Archibald, 54, crofter, widow, with Mary, 27, Alexander, 20, stonebreaker, John, 17, and a visitor, Isabella Purves, 50; schedule 7, Jane Henderson, 56, crofter, with James Parker, 18, "adopted," Andrew, Jane, 27, dressmaker, Mary Brown, 7, and Agnes Brown, 5.
  3. Mary Archibald, born October 23, 1864, Libberton, daughter of George Archibald and Ann Purves (birth index). Her census ages, 27 in 1891 and 35 in 1901, do not agree with each other; the birth date makes her 26 and 36. John Archibald, born June 16, 1873, died June 20, 1891, and Ann Archibald, née Purves, died December 10, 1897: Archibald family gravestone, Libberton.
  4. Annie P. R. Cuthbertson, daughter of Mary Archibald, died November 22, 1992, aged 94; John Cuthbertson named as "Father": gravestone, Biggar. Annie's birth entry, her surname at birth, and the date of Mary's marriage to John Cuthbertson have not yet been found.
  5. 1901 census, Libberton ED 3 (census index transcriptions): schedule 3, Shieldhill House, Alexander Archibald, 30, head, domestic gardener, wife Annie, 26, born Carnwath, and Susan Cumisky, 26, dairy maid; schedules 13 and 14, Gean Tree Cottages, Mary Archibald, 35, head, sewing mistress, alone, and James Grossart, 80, road surfaceman, with granddaughter Marion, 22; schedule 15, Lime Tree Cottage, Andrew Henderson, 25, groom, head, James Parker, 28, boarder, gamekeeper, Mary Brown, 17, and Agnes Brown, 15, nieces. Nathaniel Dunlop was at his house in Govan on census night.
  6. Lime Tree and Gean Tree cottages among Quothquan's early-1900s buildings, and Dunlop's rebuilding of village houses after 1898: Quothquan and Thankerton community local-history pages. That the row's cottages took their tree names between 1891 and 1901 is inferred from the two censuses.
  7. Gean Tree and Lime Tree "were each later converted from two houses into one": Third Statistical Account of Scotland (Lanarkshire), 1960. Gean Tree Cottage, Shieldhill Road, Quothquan: present-day address.
  8. Distance: about 199 feet in a straight line between the present-day map positions of Gean Tree Cottage (55.63941, -3.59841) and Lime Tree Cottage (55.63888, -3.59864), OpenStreetMap via Mapcarta. A parish history page reportedly states that the house still known as Geantree had earlier incorporated Lime Tree Cottage; not independently checked.
  9. A same-name case: an Edinburgh sheriff-court index lists Mary Archibald, of 2 Burns Close, High Street, Edinburgh, against John Smith, for a child born October 19, 1895 (SC39/8/64). Nothing in the listing connects her to Libberton, and it is not assumed to be the same woman.
  10. Family recollection: the author's mother, Constance Anderson Douglas, said that a gardener named Douglas took him in. The author thinks she may have been joining two stories: the gardener at Shieldhill and the Douglas family that raised him.
  11. The Royal Maternity Hospital Register of Births (LHB3/14/6, Lothian Health Services Archive) records each mother's last and future place of residence; Agnes's entry has not been seen.
  12. Not yet established: where Agnes was in service; whether Alexander Archibald was still the Shieldhill gardener in 1906; the 1911 census entries for Mary Archibald and Agnes Brown.

Chapter 11: The Gardener and His Sister

  1. Family recollection: the author's mother, Constance Anderson Douglas, said that a gardener took her father in; in the version she heard, the gardener's name was Douglas.
  2. 1891 census, Libberton ED 3, the "Castle" row, schedule 5: Ann Archibald, 54, crofter, widow; Mary, 27; Alexander, 20, stonebreaker; John, 17; a visitor, Isabella Purves, 50 (census index transcription; original page not seen).
  3. Deaths of Jane Henderson, June 8, 1891 (Quothquan monumental inscriptions), and John Archibald, June 20, 1891, and Ann Archibald, née Purves, December 10, 1897 (Archibald family gravestone, Libberton).
  4. Annie P. R. Cuthbertson, daughter of Mary Archibald: gravestone, Biggar; see the notes to Chapter 10.
  5. 1901 census, Libberton ED 3, schedule 3, Shieldhill House: Alexander Archibald, 30, head, domestic gardener; Annie, 26, wife, born Carnwath; Susan Cumisky, 26, dairy maid (census index transcription). Nathaniel Dunlop was at his house in Govan on census night. Jane Henderson's birthplace, Carnwath: 1891 census (Chapter 3).
  6. Ellen Dunlop's interest in the running of the Shieldhill estate: Quothquan local-history pages (secondary).
  7. Agnes Brown's occupation, domestic servant, and her domicile, Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar: her son's birth entry, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, registered July 4, 1907 (original image). No record found names her employer.
  8. Records that could test this chapter: Lanarkshire valuation rolls, Libberton parish, 1905–06 to 1907–08 (National Records of Scotland, VR series); Royal Maternity Hospital Register of Births, January 1905–July 1912 (LHB3/14/6, Lothian Health Services Archive), which records each mother's last and future place of residence.
  9. Not yet established: whether Alexander Archibald was still the Shieldhill gardener in 1906, and where he lived that year.

Chapter 12: James Parker

  1. 1881 census, Libberton: Jane Henderson's household, James Parker, 8, "Adopted Son," with Jane, 19, David, 14, and Andrew, 5 (census index transcription; original page not seen).
  2. 1891 census, Libberton, "Castle": Jane Henderson, 56, head; James Parker, 18, "Adopted," born Biggar, agricultural labourer; Jane, 27, daughter; Mary Brown, 7, and Agnes Brown, 5, granddaughters (census index transcription).
  3. 1901 census, Libberton ED 3, schedule 15, Lime Tree Cottage: Andrew Henderson, 25, groom, head; James Parker, 28, boarder, born Biggar, gamekeeper; Mary Brown, 17, and Agnes Brown, 15, nieces (census index transcription).
  4. Andrew Henderson: 1881 census, 5, in Jane Henderson's household; 1891, indexed as 74 (almost certainly 14); 1901, 25, groom, head of Lime Tree Cottage (census index transcriptions). "Andrew Henderson, late of Lime Tree," poet and beekeeper: Quothquan local-history page. His whereabouts after 1901 have not been traced.
  5. Other keepers in the district, 1901: Robert Arthur, 47, gamekeeper, Huntfield Lodge; Robert Clarkson, 50, gamekeeper, The Cottage, Cormiston (census index). Which estate employed James Parker is not recorded. Shieldhill appears in the 1906 shooting-tenant lists of Lyall's Sportsman's Guide (snippet only).
  6. In his 1903 marriage entry James Parker named his parents as Benjamin Parker, mason, and Jane Lawson, lady's maid, both deceased; whether the 1872 James Lawson birth entry at Biggar is his has not been settled. Another James Parker, born about 1864 at Dunsyre, lived in Quothquan with his mother, Margaret Muir, and grandmother, Lily Muir, in 1891 and 1901; whether the two men were related is not known.
  7. 1911 census, Libberton (650/3, ED 3, p. 2), schedule 10, 3 Shieldhill Mains, three rooms, April 2, 1911 (original image): James Parker, head, 38, married, gamekeeper, worker, born Lanarkshire, Biggar; Janet Parker, wife, 34, married 7 years, 3 children born alive, 3 living, born Argyllshire, Dunoon; John, son, 5, school; Euphemia, daughter, 3; Robert, son, 1; all three children born Lanarkshire, Libberton. Same page: schedule 12, Gean Tree Cottage, Andrew Rodger, 65, farmer, born Pettinain, and Jane, 46, wife; schedules 13–14, Lime Tree Cottage, George Rodger, 57, and Thomas and Mary A. H. Stoddart.
  8. Searched November 19, 2026, ScotlandsPeople indexes: no James Parker birth registered at Biggar, 1872–1874; no death 1901–1911 matching him (a "James Parker," 37, Dunfermline, 1902, 424/435, is John Parker, coal miner, on the original entry).
  9. Marriage of James Lawson Parker and Janet Crawford Stewart, August 28, 1903, at Coldstream, Carluke, after banns according to the forms of the United Free Church; officiating minister John White, St John's Church, Carluke; witnesses George Affleck and Mary Stewart; registered August 31, 1903: Statutory registers, Marriages, Carluke, 629/54 (original image). Groom: gamekeeper, bachelor, 31, usual residence Shieldhill, Biggar; father Benjamin Parker, mason (deceased); mother Jane Lawson, lady's maid (deceased). Bride: domestic servant, spinster, 24, Coldstream; father John Stewart, shepherd; mother Euphemia Stewart, M.S. Wallace.
  10. Euphemia Wallace Parker, born 1908, Libberton, 650/2, mother's maiden surname Stewart (index), confirms the identification.
  11. James Lawson, born 1872, Biggar, 623/29, no mother's maiden surname in the index (index only; entry not viewed). The identification with James Lawson Parker rests on name, year, place and his mother's name.
  12. Lanark Sheriff Court paternity index (Scottish Indexes): the two Agnes Brown cases found concern births in 1868 and 1912, not 1907.
  13. The Royal Maternity Hospital changed its form of case records in 1877; a study of its registers reports that later birth registers omitted fathers' details for children born outside marriage (Edinburgh Royal Maternity Hospital records, Lothian Health Services Archive; published hospital studies).
  14. Family recollection: the author's mother, Constance Anderson Douglas, said the father was someone very important at the estate, that Agnes lived on the estate with him, that the matter was hushed up for that reason, and that she thought he was a doctor.
  15. Nathaniel Dunlop, born Campbeltown, April 7, 1830; bought Shieldhill 1898; knighted at Buckingham Palace, July 15, 1907 (The London Gazette, July 26, 1907: "Nathaniel Dunlop, Esq., Shieldhill, Biggar"); honorary LL.D., University of Glasgow, 1907 (date from biographical sources; the university's conferral record not seen); "Sir Nathaniel Dunlop, LL.D., of Shieldhill, Biggar": Proceedings of the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland, meeting of February 12, 1912; addressed the Clyde Trustees as chairman on January 8, 1907 (cited in The River Clyde and the Clyde Burghs); died at Shieldhill, November 15, 1919: Nathaniel Dunlop, Wikipedia (citing Who's Who in Glasgow in 1909 and other sources). Widower since 1867, daughter Ellen Smith Dunlop: research notes.
  16. Will of Sir Nathaniel Dunlop, holograph, signed at Shieldhill April 13, 1919 (witnesses William Barbour, chauffeur, and Margaret Low), with a letter to his trustees of May 15, 1919, registered Books of Council and Session November 26, 1919; Lanark Sheriff Court Wills SC38/44/3, pp. 494–499 (original images, viewed November 19, 2026). The bequests name his daughter, nephews and nieces, Margaret Low ("in token of her services to my Daughter from her childhood, and to myself as sick nurse"), his secretary Agnes Low, his partner Henry Allan, charities, and "our domestic and out door servants as my Daughter may direct," £200 in all. Damage: about $300 million, property damage for the whole storm, in contemporary (1938) dollars: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory, "80th Anniversary of the Great New England Hurricane" ($300 million); Clio, "Hurricane of September 21st 1938 Historical Marker" ($306 million).
  7. High-water mark, Market House: bronze markers erected 1938 by the City of Providence Public Buildings Department and the State of Rhode Island; 1938 tide 13 ft 8½ in above mean high water, 1 ft 11¼ in above the 1815 mark of 11 ft 9¼ in: Historical Marker Database, marker 56293, and Clio entry 21735. The plaque's figure is used here, and PBS gives the same.
  8. People drowned near City Hall; storm over by about 5:30: American Heritage, August 1969. Drivers drowned in their cars: The Reformer; Salve Regina University thesis.
  9. Prudence Island lighthouse deaths: compiled 1938 death lists, US Deadly Events; widely reported. The names have not been checked against death certificates and are omitted.
  10. Looting and National Guard patrols: Clio entry 21735; PBS eyewitness testimony.
  11. Steamer Monhegan sunk at Fox Point: Rhode Island College, Kevorkian 1938 hurricane photograph collection, item 63, "'Monhegan' Sinks at Fox Point, East Side of Providence." Clio's caption spells the vessel "Mohegan."
  12. Two weeks to dig out: Urban Decay, "The Great New England Hurricane of 1938."
  13. Fox Point Hurricane Barrier: completed 1966. Army Corps of Engineers publications give conflicting dates for the start of construction (1960 and 1961 both appear).

Chapter 29: A Wedding in Alabama

  1. Birth of Eugenie Elizabeth, February 10, 1939, Attleboro, Bristol County, Massachusetts: naturalization petition 139903 (original image). Her Massachusetts birth registration has not been seen; the petition does not name her mother, and Constance is identified as the mother by the family and by the 1940 census household. That Eugenie Elizabeth was named for Eugenie Delaire Darcy and for Elizabeth (Lizzie) Douglas is a reasonable reading of the names, not a documented statement.
  2. Athenia, torpedoed by U-30 on September 3, 1939, about 250 miles northwest of Ireland, more than 1,100 passengers, 117 dead: standard accounts (e.g., Imperial War Museums). Helen's 1930 voyage on the Athenia, Glasgow, September 5, 1930: passenger list (original image).
  3. Weather, October 9, 1939: NOAA GHCN-Daily, Birmingham Airport station (daily maximum 88°F, minimum 68°F, no precipitation).
  4. Janet and Thomas Crombie at 1860 South Hamlin Avenue, Chicago: 1940 U.S. census; Janet's 1948 naturalization petition gives 1858 South Hamlin.
  5. Marriage, October 9, 1939: Jefferson County, Alabama, Marriage License Record, right-hand entry p. 409 (application, physician's certificate, bond, license and return); groom Lawrence Douglas, 32, b. Edinburgh, salesman, 1860 South Hamlin Ave, Chicago, parents Robert Douglas and Elizabeth McDonald; bride Constance Eugenie Darcy, 26, b. Providence October 12, 1912, 454 Broadway, parents Albert B. Darcy and Eugenie Delaire; bond co-signer T. B. Pickens (reading); officiant Thos. R. Lea, Judge (reading) (original image). The application's fields for number of marriage and for any divorce (when and where) are hard to read; one reading of the marriage number is "1st." No divorce date or court can be read from the entry.
  6. Jefferson County Courthouse, Holabird & Root, 1929–32; Leo Friedlander reliefs; John W. Norton murals: National Register of Historic Places, ref. 82001606.
  7. Notices, October 10, 1939: Birmingham Post (Newspapers.com image 1002405034); Birmingham Age-Herald, p. 4 (image 1001521860; the viewer labels it Post-Herald) (index entries only; text not read, so it is not known whether they report the license or the ceremony).
  8. Marriage to Helen Ena Harrison, Cook County, Illinois, September 22, 1930, license 1291873 (index); Helen's May 2, 1938 Cameronia manifest naming her husband (original image). Helen's 1950 marriage entry (Ayr, 578/1 270) states that she obtained a decree of divorce against Laurence Brown Douglas; it gives no date or court. If the decree was Scottish, the Court of Session records at the National Records of Scotland would hold it; Cook County and Rhode Island divorce records have not been searched.
  9. "2nd wife": naturalization petition 139903, U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania, dated February 11, 1943 (original image). The oath and admission followed on May 6, 1943.

Chapter 30: California

  1. Marriage, Jefferson County, Alabama, October 9, 1939: marriage license record p. 409; Laurence of 1860 South Hamlin Avenue, Chicago; Constance of 454 Broadway, Providence (original image).
  2. 1940 U.S. census, San Francisco, ED 38-259, sheet 62A, household 93, lines 12–14 (T627 roll 307); enumerated April 11, 1940; Valencia Street, house number blank; daughter born Massachusetts, age one (original image).
  3. Bond Stores: founded Cleveland 1914; Bond Stores, Inc., 1937; Times Square store 1940 (published histories). San Francisco store at Post and Kearny: Laurence's draft registration card, October 16, 1940 (original image), and 'Bond Clothes, Post and Kearny', Polk's San Francisco directory, 1944. A photograph of November 1950 (OpenSFHistory) shows Bond at Kearny and Maiden Lane.
  4. 129 Julian Avenue (built 1916, four stories, seven units) and 17 Mirabel Avenue (built 1905, two flats): San Francisco Assessor.
  5. WWII draft registration, serial 3426, order 1704, Local Board 94, 513 Valencia Street, October 16, 1940: 129 Julian Avenue; Bond Stores Inc., Post and Kearny; contact wife Constance (original image). Albert Norman Darcy's registration, Warwick, October 16, 1940: index entry only.
  6. San Francisco city directory, 1941: Lawrence L. Douglas, displayman, Bond Clothes, wife Constance E., 129 Julian; Bond Clothes, Carl Allison, manager, YUkon 0585 (original image).
  7. Re-entry permit issued Washington, June 2, 1941; departure June 20; readmitted Blaine, Washington, June 21, 1941, by stage, with wife Constance, U.S. citizen; age recorded 33; destination 17-B Mirabel (typed 'Marabel') Avenue, San Francisco (original image). The card names no children and does not say why he was in Canada.
  8. Constance Anderson Douglas's birth year. The California Birth Index (index entry only; Ancestry collection 5247, record 2634004) gives February 2, 1941, San Francisco County, mother's maiden name Darcy. Laurence's naturalization petition 139903, dated February 11, 1943 (original image), gives February 2, 1942, San Francisco. No birth certificate, hospital record, baptismal record or contemporary announcement has been found, and the April 1940 census, which lists only one daughter, is consistent with either year. The index is compiled from state birth registrations; the petition is the father's sworn statement made one or two years after the birth; neither has been checked against the certificate. A copy of the California birth certificate would settle it.
  9. Elizabeth Douglas's use of the surname Anderson: 1929 passenger lists naming 'Mrs. Elizabeth Anderson, 39 Grieve St.' as mother of both Laurence and Janet (original images). Her second marriage, to Thomas Anderson, is reported only in a family tree.

Chapter 31: Pearl Harbor: The Sirens of San Francisco

  1. Laurence in the Pittsburgh district from about September 1941 while his wife, Constance Eugenie Darcy Douglas, remained in San Francisco: family recollection, as told to the author. Petition witnesses David Hunter and Frank Holliday knew him from September 1941: naturalization petition 139903 (original image). Neither source places either spouse on December 7, 1941, or gives a reason for the separation.
  2. Reports reached San Francisco at 11:29 a.m.; volunteers by 1 p.m.; Mayor Rossi's state of emergency; 385 at Northern Station by 3:30; tunnels, airport, Golden Gate Bridge searches, warning shots at Bay Bridge painters; wardens shouting 'Turn out the lights'; 700 enlistments on December 8; the hour-long blackout of December 9 and the death of Ann Stewart; Air Raid Rules for eight days; garden hoses; complaints to the mayor; Twin Peaks siren; Farallon submarine report: San Francisco Chronicle, 'SF at war: a time of air raids, blackouts and joining the effort', 2016.
  3. First air raid and blackout at 6:15 p.m., December 8; Mayor Rossi's emergency proclamation: Museum of the City of San Francisco, 'San Francisco during World War II: 1940–1941' chronology. Four alarms on the night of December 8: San Francisco Chronicle, 'Post-Pearl Harbor photos show San Francisco bracing for war', and the December 9, 1941 headline.
  4. Thirty-odd planes from San Jose to Mare Island; the only sirens on the Ferry Building and two small bridges; neon signs on time-locks: Warfare History Network, 'Pearl Harbor Jitters', quoting Newsweek.

Chapter 32: Citizen Douglas

  1. Petition for naturalization 139903, U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania, Pittsburgh, dated February 11, 1943: residence 612 California Avenue, Avalon; display manager, Bond Stores; description; last foreign residence Ayr; emigrated from Glasgow; arrival Detroit September 15, 1929, as Lawrence Brown; wife Constance Darcy, '2nd wife', married Birmingham October 9, 1939; children Eugenie Elizabeth and Constance Anderson, both residing with him (original image). February 11, 1943 is the date of the petition; the San Francisco depositions followed on March 3 and the oath and admission on May 6, 1943. The 1929 passenger list and border card give Dunfermline as his last residence and Greenock as his port of embarkation (original images).
  2. The petition's date for Constance Anderson Douglas's birth (February 2, 1942) conflicts with the California Birth Index (February 2, 1941): see the note on her birth year to Chapter 30.
  3. Witnesses David Hunter, machinist, and Frank Holliday, clerk, knew him from September 1941: petition 139903 (original image; witnesses' addresses read provisionally).
  4. 612 California Avenue, Avalon (two-story brick, c. 1900, office with apartments over): Allegheny County assessment.
  5. Depositions of William Howard Vahlkamp and Betty Johnstone Sherwood, San Francisco, March 3, 1943 (original image).
  6. Oath of allegiance and order granting petition 139903 and admitting him to citizenship, May 6, 1943: oath and admission page of the petition (original image).
  7. Albert Blake Darcy's registration, Local Board Kent 2, Warwick, April 27, 1942 (original image).
  8. Final surrender of German forces at Stalingrad, February 2, 1943; Axis surrender in Tunisia, May 13, 1943: standard histories.

Chapter 33: Home to Rhode Island

  1. Obituary, Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3: work for Pawtucket firms during the previous fifteen years (original image).
  2. Pawtucket city directory, 1947, p. 154: 97 Magill Street, wife Constance E., window dresser (original image).
  3. Providence city directory, 1950, p. 214: Lawrence B. (Constance), 148 General Street (original image); 1951, 1953, 1955: display worker, 148 General Street (index and transcription entries).
  4. Magill Street housing (e.g. no. 79, three-family, 1920): Pawtucket assessor; downtown Pawtucket stores: Downtown Pawtucket Historic District nomination.
  5. Norma Douglas: named as Miss Norma Douglas of Providence in her father's obituary, March 11, 1961; her birth date and place have not been established from a record. The daughters' schooling at St. Mary's Academy, Bay View: family recollection.
  6. Hurricane Carol damage totals for New England (homes, automobiles, boats destroyed): U.S. Weather Bureau figures as reported in National Weather Service summaries of the storm.
  7. Death of Margaret Jane Darcy, September 10, 1942, 60 Blake Street, Shawomet, Warwick; informant her son Albert B. Darcy of the same address: death certificate 159 (original image).
  8. Albert Norman Darcy, d. October 1, 1954, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5, lot 84: Catholic cemetery-office index.
  9. Albert Blake Darcy, d. November 4, 1957, Mount Saint Mary Cemetery, Pawtucket, section 9, lot 278: cemetery-office index; grave marker.
  10. Ada Elizabeth Townsend or Harrison, d. June 10, 1952, of 1a Inverkar Road, Ayr: Probate Calendar, 1952, p. 982.
  11. Naturalization oaths: Thomas Crombie, petition 327632, September 9, 1947; Janet Crombie, petition 329111, March 16, 1948 (original images).

Chapter 34: The Last House

  1. Providence city directories 1956, 1959: Laurence B. and Constance E., 644 River Avenue, display work (directory index entries).
  2. Providence city directory, 1960, p. 287: displayman, Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket, home 644 River (original image).
  3. Providence city directory, 1961, p. 259: window displays at 644 River Avenue; Constance E., nurse, Roger Williams General Hospital (original image).
  4. Laurence's dress, love of reading and heavy smoking; Constance Eugenie Darcy Douglas's heavy smoking: family recollection, as told to the author.
  5. Constance Eugenie Darcy Douglas's nursing training: Rhode Island School of Practical Nursing, per her obituary.
  6. Sister Mary Laurene, O.P., St. Dominic's Convent, Blauvelt, N.Y.; Mrs. Constance Garceau of Warwick; Miss Norma Douglas of Providence: obituary, Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). Dates of Eugenie Elizabeth Douglas's entry and profession have not been established from a record.
  7. Marriage of Jessie E. Crombie and Ronald H. Power, Cook County, September 20, 1958 (index).
  8. Surgeon General's report, Smoking and Health, January 11, 1964.

Chapter 35: The Ninth of March

  1. Lung cancer; the family's not knowing of it until he was hospitalized; his sudden admission: recollection of his daughter Constance Anderson Douglas, the author's mother. His death certificate, which would give the certified cause, has not been obtained. His smoking, his dress, his love of reading and his nickname "Doug": family recollection.
  2. Death, Thursday, March 9, 1961, St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, after a brief illness; home 644 River Avenue; age 53; born Edinburgh, Scotland; late parents Robert and Elizabeth (Anderson) Douglas; Bond Clothing Co., own display business, fifteen years for Pawtucket firms; survivors as quoted: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). The identification of Sister Mary Laurene as Eugenie Elizabeth Douglas and of Mrs. Constance Garceau as Constance Anderson Douglas is family knowledge.
  3. Age at death calculated from the Edinburgh birth entry (June 14, 1907).
  4. St. Joseph's Hospital, 21 Peace Street: dedicated March 20, 1892, and opened in April 1892 as St. Joseph's Hospital for Incurables in the former Harris mansion; cornerstone of a new building laid July 2, 1893; west wing completed October 8, 1930; expansion 1954; Harris mansion razed March 1962: hospital and diocesan histories (secondary).
  5. 56 Dartmouth Avenue and 21 Peace Street lie on the same assessor's plat (44): Providence tax roll.
  6. The Mason Building, 165–169 Weybosset Street (1903); the Outlet Company across the street at 168–176 Weybosset: Downtown Providence historic-district and preservation records. Laurence's workplace at 165 Weybosset: Providence city directories, 1937 and 1938.
  7. Funeral announced for 10 a.m., Monday, March 13, 1961, Ruth E. Urquhart, 812 Greenwich Avenue, Warwick: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). This is an advance announcement; no separate record of the service itself has been seen.
  8. Burial, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5, lot 84: Laurence's own interment record has not been seen. The burial rests on the gravestone, known from a photograph in an Ancestry member gallery (inscriptions: Laurence B. Douglas 1907–1961; Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994), and on the Catholic cemeteries' index, which places Albert Norman Darcy (died October 1, 1954) and Constance Darcy Douglas (1994, grave 3) in section 5, lot 84.

Epilogue: The Names He Carried

  1. Warwick city directory 1963: Constance, widow of Lawrence B., nurse, 119 Phillips Avenue (original image). Warwick city directory 1965: 1292 Post Road, nurse, Briarcliffe Health Center, Johnston (text finding; page image not checked).
  2. Constance Darcy Douglas's practical-nurse training, eight years at Cranston General Hospital, retirement in 1974, residence on Sixth Street, East Greenwich, and St. Francis de Sales Church; death at Rhode Island Hospital; three daughters, twelve grandchildren, two great-grandchildren: her 1994 obituary, seen only as a partial reproduction attached to an online memorial; the original newspaper page has not been seen. Her pleasant nature and the name "Nan": family recollection.
  3. Eugenie E. DeLaire Darcy, 1894–1966, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5: Find a Grave memorial 149385784 (secondary).
  4. Death of Constance Darcy Douglas, April 12, 1994; burial Saint Ann Cemetery, section 5, lot 84, grave 3: Catholic cemeteries' burial index. Stone inscription Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994: member-gallery photograph of the gravestone.
  5. Janet Crombie, b. April 29, 1900, d. December 1979, last residence Maywood, Illinois: Social Security Death Index, record 13228117 (index). Duchess of Bedford manifest, arrived September 13, 1929: see Chapter 21. Marriage record giving 1860 South Hamlin Avenue, Chicago: see Chapter 29.
  6. Betty Crombie Mitchell, d. June 23, 2009, Minneapolis: Minnesota Death Index; Star Tribune, June 25, 2009 (index). Jessie Crombie, d. December 12, 2015, Poplar Grove, Illinois: U.S. Obituary Collection, Janesville Gazette, December 15, 2015 (index).
  7. Death of Helen Ena Pirie, March 16, 1973, 10:10 a.m., 1a Inverkar Road, Ayr; marital status married; spouses (1) Laurence Brown Douglas, grocer (assistant), (2) George Rees [sic] Pirie, sales assistant, departmental stores; father Richard Harrison, captain, Royal Scots Fusiliers (deceased); mother Ada Harrison, M.S. Townsend (deceased); cause I(a) cerebral thrombosis, (b) arteriosclerosis, certified by G. W. Paterson; informant George Pirie, widower, 1a Inverkar Road; registered at Ayr, March 16, 1973: Statutory registers, Deaths, Ayr, 680/196, indexed as Helen Ena Douglas (original image). The entry gives her date of birth as June 26, 1904; her age, 65, and the India baptism index give 1907. The death entry spells the second husband's name "George Rees Pirie"; the marriage entry has "George Lees Pirrie," his mother's maiden surname being Lees.
  8. Marriage of George Lees Pirrie and Helen Ena Harrison, August 11, 1950, Ayr, after banns according to the forms of the Church of Scotland; registered August 12, 1950: Statutory registers, Marriages, Ayr, 578/1 270, indexed as Helen Ena Douglas (original image). Groom: 36, grocer's assistant, widower, 20 New Road, Ayr; father Andrew Pirrie, journeyman bread baker (deceased); mother Ann Pirrie, M.S. Lees. Bride: 42, secretary, National Coal Board, "formerly married to Laurence Brown Douglas, against whom she obtained Decree of Divorce," 1a Inverkar Road, Ayr; father Richard Harrison, captain, Royal Scots Fusiliers (retired); mother Ada Harrison, M.S. Townsend. Witnesses James Pirrie, 12 New Road, Ayr, and Helen M[illar?], 20 New Road, Ayr. The date and court of the divorce are not given.
  9. Helen E. Douglas, alien registration A4384659, Newton, Massachusetts, registered between August 1940 and March 1944 (exact date not known); companion index entry Helen E. Harrison: alien-registration index (index only; her AR-2 form has not been seen). National Archives A-file A4384659, "Helen Harrison," b. June 26, 1907, India: National Archives catalog description.
  10. Alexander Edward Harrison, d. August 26, 1966, of 9 Blenheim Gardens, Aveley, Essex: England and Wales Probate Calendar, 1966, p. 195 (original image).
  11. Marriage of Agnes McGarth Brown and Thomas McKenzie, 1911 (original register image). Daughters Mary and Jean: Thomas McKenzie's First World War army service papers (original image). Agnes's portrait: Ancestry member galleries; the provenance description is the sharer's, not independently verified.
  12. Laurence in Pennsylvania from about September 1941: his naturalization witnesses' acquaintance with him from that month (petition 139903, original image) and family knowledge. Where each spouse was on December 7, 1941, is not separately documented.
  13. The pocket watch and the word "Edinburgh" inside its case: in the author's possession.
